solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rail is straddled by kid

indicators.note: being straddled means having something sit across you on both sides, so the word is goes inside

parts.note: to kid is to tease, which is to banter

explanation.surface: A child sits astride a railing, as kids do.
explanation.definitionFit: A banister is the handrail running up the side of a staircase.

clue.text: Progenitors going up and down plain

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: both a pa and a parent are progenitors, one read up and the other down
the progenitors read the normal way down the grid give a parent, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: Ancestors moving up and down a flat expanse.
explanation.walkthrough: Progenitors supplies two pieces: PA going up (AP) and PARENT read the normal way down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means plain, clear or obvious to see.

clue.text: The writer's after moving type of verb

indicators.note: after puts the writer piece behind the travelling piece

parts.note: in transit means on the move
the writer is I, and the writer has is I've

explanation.surface: Someone working out which kind of verb a writer's sentence needs.
explanation.definitionFit: An intransitive verb takes no direct object, as with sleep or arrive.

clue.text: Perform just right, spinning around in Hamlet?

indicators.note: spinning turns the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: a pat answer is apt, just right

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the next word

parts.note: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark, a Dane
C is short for circa, around

explanation.surface: An actor playing Hamlet spins round on stage, timing it perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags Hamlet as an example of a Dane, not the play.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap-dance is to perform a dance with metal-tipped shoes striking the floor.

clue.text: Hastened to fire rifle

parts.note: hastened means hurried, ran
to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off to shoot a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: Rifle is a verb here, to search through and plunder, not a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search it thoroughly and steal, to plunder it.

clue.text: That lady in the bath is a high-up leader

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Bath is a spa town, so the bath suggests a spa
her is that lady, a woman

explanation.surface: A woman lounging in a bath turns out to be someone important.
explanation.walkthrough: High-up suggests a VIP; it means a guide high in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas from Nepal guide climbers up the Himalayas, leading at great altitude.

clue.text: List from the two of us, very informally

parts.note: the two of us is me and you; this piece gives the me
very informally and you is shortened to 'n' U, as in text speak

explanation.surface: A list drawn up by a couple, put very casually.
explanation.walkthrough: Me and you written very casually becomes ME 'N' U.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is a list of the dishes available in a restaurant.

clue.text: IT system with two numbers, the second raised

parts.note: ether is a number, something that numbs, an anaesthetic

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means the second number is read upwards

parts.note: the second of the two numbers is ten

explanation.surface: A computer system using a pair of figures, the latter increased.
explanation.walkthrough: Number is read as numb-er, an anaesthetic such as ether; the second number, ten, goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethernet is the standard technology for wired local computer networks.

clue.text: Notice books, bagging present that's tacky

indicators.note: to bag something is to capture it, so the first pieces hold the next one inside them

parts.note: a notice is an advertisement, AD
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A notice with books stuck to it is still sticky from glue.
explanation.walkthrough: Tacky here means sticky, not vulgar: the definition hides behind its commoner sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adherent sticks or clings, just as tacky glue is sticky to the touch.

clue.text: Pickle lids turned the wrong way

indicators.note: turned the wrong way says the word for lids is read backwards

parts.note: lids are tops of jars

explanation.surface: Someone screws the pickle jar lids back on the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: Pickle is not the food but a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a pickle is to be in a spot, a tight or awkward situation.

clue.text: Newly share out wine getting one's praise

parts.note: red is a colour of wine
one is I, and I's is one's
a tribute is an expression of praise

explanation.surface: Wine is handed round again while someone gets compliments.
explanation.definitionFit: To redistribute is to divide up and hand out again in a fresh way.

clue.text: The scandal of fees charged in this capital market?

parts.note: billings are the amounts invoiced, fees charged
-gate added to a word names a scandal, after Watergate

explanation.surface: A scandal over overcharging in a London trading hall.
explanation.walkthrough: BILLINGSGATE is London's famous fish market, whose porters gave its name to foul language.
explanation.definitionFit: Billingsgate is a wholesale fish market in London, the capital.

clue.text: Standard sports news being shown

parts.note: PE is physical education, school sports
N stands for new, and doubling it makes the plural, news
a film being shown is on

explanation.surface: The sports news is being broadcast as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: Standard is not 'usual' but a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow flag, and a standard is a flag or banner.

clue.text: Clergyman's a boring Charlie?

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the a goes inside the comedian's name

parts.note: Charlie Chaplin, the silent film comedian

explanation.surface: A clergyman is called a dull fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Boring seems to mean dull, but it means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a priest or minister attached to an institution such as a college or regiment.

clue.text: Walk out, perhaps, then run forward

parts.note: a walkout is one kind of strike
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone stages a walkout and then dashes ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Forward is a noun here, a football position, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a striker is an attacking forward whose job is scoring goals.

clue.text: Resort on rocks, one in Italy

indicators.note: rocks means shakes up, so these letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A seaside resort set on rocky cliffs in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Resort looks like the definition; it is anagram fodder, and the definition is one in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrento is a resort town on the Bay of Naples, a seaside place in Italy.

clue.text: Boater, say, welcoming some home

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in as a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a boater is a kind of straw hat
a bit means some, a small amount

explanation.surface: A boater welcomes a few guests into their home on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Boater looks like a person in a boat; it is a straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home of an animal or plant.

clue.text: Old English walls cold in one church

indicators.note: walls means encloses, so the cold letter is put inside

parts.note: Anglian is the Old English dialect of the Angles
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: An old English church whose walls are cold inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglican describes belonging to the Church of England or its sister churches.

clue.text: Maybe a mite cheeky, keeping a rumpus up

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the a is held inside

parts.note: arch means mischievous, cheeky

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a din is a noisy rumpus

explanation.surface: A slightly cheeky child is causing a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: A mite looks like 'a little', but it is the tiny creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Mites, like spiders and ticks, are arachnids, eight-legged creatures.

clue.text: Vocabulary of large person who used to be revered?

parts.words: person who used to be revered
parts.note: an ex-icon is a former idol, once revered

explanation.surface: The words used by a big, once-famous figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is the stock of words in a language or used by a person.

clue.text: Spreading manure? It's what some on farm do

indicators.note: spreading scatters the letters of the words around into a new order

explanation.surface: Muck-spreading is a farm job, so a farmer might say so.
explanation.walkthrough: Spreading manure is real farm work, which makes it a neat disguise for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows and sheep chew the cud, which is what to ruminate literally means.

clue.text: Tech company needs time to make program

parts.note: Apple is the technology company

explanation.surface: A tech firm needs time to build software.
explanation.definitionFit: An applet is a small application program, often run inside another.

clue.text: Funny fellow fed on guava's skin

indicators.note: on says the second piece follows the first
the skin of a fruit is its outside, so the first and last letters

parts.note: a fed is an FBI agent, a G-man

explanation.surface: A comedian eats guava peel as part of the act.
explanation.walkthrough: Fed looks like the past tense of feed; it is US slang for a federal agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A gagman is a comedian or a writer of jokes for others.

clue.text: Bold to participate in revolt, seizing power

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the joined words hold the letter inside

parts.note: to enter a contest is to participate in it
a rising is a revolt
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Joining an uprising that seizes power takes courage.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprising person shows initiative and daring, readiness to take bold risks.

clue.text: Maybe saw money getting raised

indicators.note: in a down entry getting raised means the word is read upwards

parts.note: loot is slang for money

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone saw money being collected.
explanation.walkthrough: Saw looks like the past of see; it is the cutting implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is one example of a tool, as are hammers and chisels.

clue.text: A schoolkid's problem covered by Isaac Newton

indicators.note: covered by says the letters sit concealed within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A schoolchild struggles with physics homework on Newton.
explanation.walkthrough: The problem looks like a physics exercise, but it is a skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Spots on the face are a common complaint of teenagers at school.

clue.text: See you at that party hosting stars

parts.note: at that means as well, too

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so the party word holds the constellation inside

parts.note: a do is a party
Leo is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: A farewell to someone heading off to a celebrity party.
explanation.walkthrough: TOODLE-OO is a jaunty old British way of saying goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual farewells said when parting from someone.

clue.text: Chic nurse no hugs console

indicators.note: hugs means wraps around, so the word no goes on both sides of the next pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable, chic
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: A stylish nurse declines to hug and comforts someone instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Console looks like a verb, to comfort; it is a games machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Nintendo makes games consoles such as the Switch, so the brand stands for one.
